Per WHO diagnostic criteria, *a single cardinal sign is sufficient to diagnose leprosy*; here, *two* are present: (i) sensory loss in a skin lesion (anaesthetic hypopigmented patch), and (ii) peripheral neuropathy (ulnar sensory deficit confirmed by electrophysiology). The 1-year history of upper-body/face rash and palmar paresthesia is temporally and topographically consistent with early leprosy — particularly paucibacillary forms, which typically present with few (1–5), well-defined, hypoesthetic/hypopigmented lesions and asymmetric or early nerve involvement (e.g., ulnar).
